notes: Every documented OpenAPI operation must be consumed by the frontend, mechanically derivable as a springdoc alias duplicate, or listed here with a category and a reason.
bff-route-handler and non-browser-consumer entries are machine-verified: an evidence file must exist and reference the operation path suffix. A category label alone proves nothing.
unwired entries are real debt. expected.unwiredMax is a monotonic ratchet — raising it is a visible diff, never a silent exception.
Alias duplicates (springdoc _N suffixes over multi-path @RequestMapping) are derived, never listed. Listing one is an error.

AXIS 2 (screen reachability): consumed on axis 1 only means a production TypeScript module calls the operation. Axis 2 additionally checks that the service method wrapping that call site is invoked from outside services/ and tests — the case that first exposed the gap was deleteRespondent, whose only caller was its own unit test.

Axis 2 keeps no exception list on purpose: 77 entries would become a drawer (H2). It is a single monotonic ratchet (expected.screenOrphanMax) and prints the full offending list on failure, mirroring status-color-guard.

Axis 2 is deliberately lenient, following UnreachableServiceLinter: a method counts as reachable if `.name(` appears anywhere in non-service production code. Common names may pass by collision — that direction misses violations rather than inventing them.

entries.note: Next route handler proxies login server-side so the refresh token never reaches browser JavaScript; the browser calls /api/auth/login, not the backend operation.
Same BFF boundary as login — the route handler clears the HttpOnly cookies it set.
Token reissue runs server-side in the route handler; the refresh token is never exposed to the client bundle.

InformalSanctionApiController serves this domain at /api/v1/informal-sanctions (aliased at /api/v1/admin/system/ism). DEC-OPS-040 consolidated the ISM screen into /approvals, which calls ApprovalApiController instead; DEC-OPS-053 then removed the dead IsmAdminService. Both controllers wrap the same InformalSanctionService, so this is a superseded surface, not a missing feature. Neither controller is a subset of the other (approvals adds processed/task-types, ISM keeps detail/update), so retiring it is a backend design decision — see GAP-WIRING-001.

Application-level liveness surface with no wired probe — docker-compose healthchecks use /actuator/health instead. Decide whether to point a probe here or drop the endpoint.
Forced-500 diagnostic, bean-excluded under @Profile("!prod"). Invoked by hand when verifying GlobalExceptionHandler; no automated consumer.

Public self-signup has no screen — this product provisions accounts through admin user management. The endpoint stays frozen by SignupContractLinter (privilege-escalation regression guard) rather than deleted.
Duplicate-id check exists only to serve the unwired signup flow above; it becomes reachable if signup gets a screen.

Respondent register write path, deliberately unwired. tb_srvy_rspdnt holds personal data (name, gender, birthdate, phone) and is NOT linked to survey results by id — tb_srvy_rslt carries only rspns_nm as a string (V2_0). No code path creates respondent rows, so the register is structurally empty. Wiring a create form would open a new personal-data entry surface with no downstream consumer; that is a product decision, not a wiring gap.
Respondent detail — same deliberate hold as createRespondent (personal data, register unlinked from results).
Respondent update — same deliberate hold as createRespondent (personal data, register unlinked from results).
Survey template detail. The template screen lists and writes templates but never opens one by id. Its /api/v1/surveys alias is derived from this entry, not listed separately.
Self-notification creation for the authenticated principal. Admin dispatch to other users goes through the separate /admin/notifications/dispatch operation (DEC-OPS-042), which is wired.
Notification detail — the notification centre renders from the list response and never fetches a single item.
Single-notification delete — the centre exposes mark-as-read and bulk paths only.
Satisfaction rating update. ADR-0011 retired anonymous satisfaction and left edit/delete as authenticated owner-or-admin, but no screen offers editing an existing rating yet.
Admin moderation delete for a satisfaction rating; no moderation screen exists.
Flat schedule list. The schedule screens query the department-scoped endpoints instead.
Per-user login policy creation. The restored /admin/security/login-policy screen (DEC-OPS-024) reads and updates policies but has no create path.
Menu creation candidates by authority code; the menu admin screen builds its tree from the standard menu list.
User-facing connection statistics; the stats screens consume the admin statistics operations.
Institution code detail. The institution screen shows list rows only — related to GAP-CODE-001, where the receive-log to ledger path is still undecided.
